account: It is day 1, nine in the morning, and I am in my office after attending the eight o'clock office hours. Today's appointments include a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at fifteen hundred, office at sixteen-thirty, and an approved great hall lighting inspection with the builder at eighteen hundred before returning home at nineteen hundred. The unusual thread is the recent attention to lighting: newly installed hall lanterns and cheerful lights at the bakery. The secretary reports that the builder calls the hall inspection a routine review of lanterns and their coverage, with no particular problem reported. The neighbour says the bakery lights are simply to brighten it, and offered to walk with me to the hall today. The neighbour explicitly said this is the same inspection the builder arranged, not another meeting. I have not yet obtained the inspection's attendance or further details directly from the builder. Yesterday I also saw freight carrying bread, but learned no clear dockside news from him. This morning I heard the baker shouting in the distance, but could not make out the words, so I cannot infer what it concerned. The secretary has received no letters or petitions and has reported no verified unusual news. I still have a feeling that something may be going on without me, but I have no evidence of a hidden gathering or purpose. The stated purpose of the lighting work is ordinary improvement and inspection; my appointments, particularly tea and the hall visit, should give me opportunities to learn more firsthand.
